points.text: CT-KV is Prefix Tuning with demonstration-KV initialization plus borrowed LOO masking; moderate novelty
ICO framework is a taxonomy defined to fit TTT and Context Tuning; little insight
Related work thin on KV distillation, task vectors, gist tokens; no comparisons
Efficiency gap partly systems artifact from different batch sizes and checkpointing
No iteration- or FLOPs-matched comparison; measured speedup not reconciled with complexity analysis
Memory not reported; fewer-parameters claim not quantified against same-rank LoRA
Inference cost of long optimized KV prefix not discussed
Efficiency evidence thin at realistic model sizes; NLP-LR uses GPT-2 and different hardware
Unclear whether hyperparameter selection uses validation split or evaluation queries
Tuning budgets differ: CT-KV swept, TTT uses original settings; budget parity needed
ARC is a single run; differences of 1-2 tasks over-interpreted
Dropping LOO on ARC is post hoc, chosen on evaluation set
Claim that initialization lowers standard deviation untested
Table 4 retrieval diagnostic does not show KV cache fails to encode task
No experiment links Table 4 deficit to CT-KV gains
Alternative explanations (more gradient steps, label/format calibration) untested
Missing plain few-shot LoRA fine-tuning baseline without leave-one-out
Missing ICL baselines with more/better-selected demonstrations or calibration
Missing ICL + CoT baseline on BBH
NLP-LR with GPT-2 has near-zero-shot ICL; gains uninformative for modern LLMs
Benchmarks mostly multiple-choice with small k; generation and larger models untested
MetaICL comparison across different regimes and base models is loosely informative
TTT evaluated without augmentation or voting, weaker than original recipe
Table 1/2 ARC entries easy to misread; unexplained Table 10 row
Tens of millions of trainable parameters not 'lightweight'; framing should be calibrated
No variance or significance for TTT vs CT-KV differences
Figure 1 described only in text
Incremental: mainly replaces LoRA in TTT with prompt/prefix tuning
Prior few-shot prompt/prefix tuning initialization work not discussed
Model-benchmark pairing arbitrary, hampering cross-task comparison
Some benchmarks such as NLP-LR are dated for modern LLM evaluation
Requires explicit (x,y) pairs, no CoT; limits use on math or coding
Requiring curated few-shot pairs at test time reduces real-world relevance
Mechanism mainly an improved initialization of prompt/prefix tuning
TTT+CT-KV presented as contribution; need clearer separation and ablations isolating gains
Robustness to label noise suggests method not learning from labels
Leave-one-out masking implementation underspecified
Too incremental relative to TTT
No analysis of why gains over prompt/prefix tuning (initialization vs LOO)
Test-time per-task tuning trade-off (overfitting, parameter copies) questionable vs ICL paradigm
No comparison with optimized natural-language prompts at comparable effort
Should compare with traditional fine-tuning methods
